title: Mother's Secret
next_chapter_hook: At the moment Chen Ji believed he had touched upon the truth, the final mural on the wall suddenly illuminated—a sealed memory, and the last words his mother left in this world.

text.content:
When that name came from the consciousness of the Eye of Heavenly Secrets, Chen Ji froze—the ancestor of the Chen bloodline was actually the mastermind behind everything.

His fingers trembled slightly, the cold touch at his fingertips reminding him this was no dream. The ancestor who had been revered for ten thousand years was actually a chess player treating all living beings as pieces. And him? Was he, Chen Ji, merely a piece on that chessboard?

"No..." Chen Ji murmured, his voice echoing in the empty ruins, "If I am a piece, then what is Mother?"

Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. He could feel the Tianji Record warming against his chest, as if responding to its master's emotional turmoil.

Since he had come this far, there was no turning back. He walked forward slowly, stepping into the doorway that emitted a faint glow. The murals on both sides of the corridor gradually became clear, their time-eroded patterns presenting themselves before his eyes—not the wars and killings he had imagined, but the figure of a woman.

That silhouette gradually merged with his memories of his mother's outline, causing Chen Ji's heart to pound violently.

At the end of the corridor was a modest stone chamber, its four walls covered with dense inscriptions. In the center of the ground stood a stone altar, with an already dried inkstone on it and a yellowed silk scroll beside it.

Chen Ji's steps halted at the threshold. His gaze fell upon the stone wall in the center of the chamber—a portrait of a woman was carved there, her eyebrows gentle, her smile serene, exactly like his mother's appearance in his memories.

Only, the mother in the portrait wore a plain white gown with a crystal jade hairpin in her hair. That temperament was entirely different from the ordinary, gentle woman in his memories—it was the transcendent beauty of one who had surpassed mortal limits.

dialogue.content:
"Mother... who are you?"

Chen Ji's voice echoed in the stone chamber, carrying an uncontrollable tremor. He walked slowly toward the stone wall, his fingertips gently touching the portrait—the warm, smooth stone texture actually carried a faint warmth, as if spanning ten thousand years to respond to him.

text.content:
The moment Chen Ji's fingers touched the portrait, a slight vibration came from deep within the stone wall. A glimmer of light flickered in the eyes of the woman in the portrait—soft and warm, like his mother's gaze when she sang him to sleep in his deepest memories.

The silk scroll on the stone altar fluttered without wind, slowly unfurling. Chen Ji lowered his head to look—the silk scroll was covered with delicate characters, densely packed—in his mother's handwriting, he could never be mistaken.

Only, the writing style of these characters was entirely different from the present era, more like... ancient seal script from ten thousand years ago.

Chen Ji steadied his emotions and began to decipher those ancient seal characters. The handwriting was delicate yet powerful, each stroke containing some indescribable emotion.

"My son Chen Ji, if you can read these characters, it means Mother's plan was not in vain."

Just this single line was enough to moisten Chen Ji's eyes. That ordinary, gentle woman, the one who hummed lullabies at his bedside every night, the one who silently applied medicine for him when he was bullied by fellow disciples—had she foreseen this reunion ten thousand years ago?

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's hand trembled slightly as his fingertips brushed those delicate characters. He wanted to say something, but his throat felt blocked, unable to utter a single word.

"Mother is not an ordinary mortal, but one of the inheritors of the Heavenly Secrets lineage from ten thousand years ago. The cycle of heaven and earth turns, catastrophe approaches; Mother used her remaining body to reincarnate, only to await a child capable of inheriting the Tianji Record."

The characters flickered in the firelight, and Chen Ji's tears finally fell.

text.content:
The characters on the silk scroll continued, unveiling more dust-shrouded secrets.

"Elder Chen Tiangming was Mother's mentor. Ten thousand years ago, he entrusted the Tianji Record to me, instructing me to seek the true destined one. Ji'er, you are the answer Mother has sought for ten thousand years."

Chen Ji finally understood everything. His mother was not an ordinary mortal, but a crucial piece in a grand strategy laid out ten thousand years ago. She had traversed reincarnation cycles in her reincarnated form, all just to await his birth.

And his years of being a "trash" disciple, enduring in seclusion—was that also within Mother's calculations?

However, the silk scroll did not end there.

"Mother found your sister Chen Nian in the Holy Sect. She was not kidnapped, but arranged by Mother—she is the Heavenly Fate Lock Key, capable of interfering with the Tianji Record's foresight. This is the final trump card Mother left for you."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Chen Nian was not taken by the Holy Sect, but sent there by Mother? His sister's vague precognitive ability was not coincidental, but a key carefully forged?

How much more was there that he did not know?

choice.prompt: Faced with the shocking truth left by his mother, Chen Ji must make a choice—continue digging into the truth, or first process these impacts?

choices.description: There seemed to be unfinished content at the end of the silk scroll. Chen Ji wanted to know what other words his mother had left unsaid.
choices.visible_cost: May face even more cruel truths
choices.risk_hint: Some truths may be heavier than imagined

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath and flipped the silk scroll to the end. As expected, on the back of the last page were a few lines of small characters covered by faint ink traces—words his mother had left with special ink, appearing only at specific moments.

He held the silk scroll close to the firelight, and those small characters gradually emerged under the catalysis of temperature: "If one day you meet someone named Chen Tiangming, tell him that at the end of reincarnation, Mother has been waiting for him."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's hand trembled violently.

Chen Tiangming—that was the first residual soul he encountered in Chen Xuan's ruins, the original inheritor of the Tianji Record. And his mother's words clearly told him: there was affection between her and Chen Tiangming that transcended master-disciple bonds.

"So... Mother is the 'her' mentioned by Chen Tiangming前辈?"

choices.description: Successive truths left Chen Ji mentally exhausted; he needed time to process all of this.

text.content:
Chen Ji slowly sat down on the ground, his back against the cold stone wall. His hands held the silk scroll, his knuckles white from the force.

For ten thousand years, he thought he was an abandoned waste, losing his mother as a child and his father disappearing, enduring endless humiliation within the sect. He thought everything about him was forced upon him, thought his trash persona was merely a means of survival.

Yet he never imagined he had long been the most important piece on his mother's chessboard—and the one most carefully protected.

dialogue.content:
"Mother..."

Chen Ji called out softly, his voice choked. In this moment, he was no longer that calculating trash Chen, no longer that secret manipulator who intervened in the world—he was merely a child who had lost his mother for years, finally finding her traces in the dust of ten thousand years.

text.content:
A long silence fell over the stone chamber, only Chen Ji's suppressed breathing echoing. After an unknown time, he finally raised his head, his gaze regaining clarity.

Even if Mother had laid out a chess game spanning ten thousand years for him, he could not merely be a protected piece. The threat of the Eye of Heavenly Secrets remained unresolved, his sister Chen Nian still suffered in the Holy Sect, and if he wanted to protect those he cared about, he must become stronger.

He carefully stored the silk scroll in his chest, his gaze falling once more on the portrait on the stone wall. This time, he noticed a line of small characters below the portrait, cleverly hidden within the folds of the woman's skirt.

"Ji'er, Mother left something beside Chen Nian. It will appear when you truly need it. Remember, you are not alone."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. Mother left something beside Chen Nian? Was it some kind of protective talisman, or something even more crucial? He recalled the blurry vision when he used the Tianji Record to foresee Chen Nian—at that time, he had simply thought Chen Nian's presence interfered with the foresight, but now considering it, perhaps Mother's seal was also at work.

At this moment, a slight vibration came from deep within the stone chamber. That portrait actually moved slowly aside, revealing a hidden compartment. Within the compartment lay a translucent jade pendant—the shape of the pendant was exactly what he had seen around his mother's neck when he was a child.

Only, the pendant in his memories was warm and smooth, while this one emanated a faint chill, as if containing some powerful force.

dialogue.content:
The moment Chen Ji reached out and picked up the jade pendant, a wave of cool energy instantly shot from his palm into his meridians. That sensation was both familiar and foreign, like his mother's tenderness when she stroked his head in the past, yet carrying a solemnity that transcended the mortal realm.

On the jade pendant, two ancient runes appeared in the light—the characters "Heavenly Secrets."

"This is..." Chen Ji's voice trembled slightly, "Mother's life-bound artifact?"

text.content:
At this moment, the Tianji Record in Chen Ji's embrace suddenly grew hot. That fragment actually flew out on its own, facing the jade pendant across the distance. Two rays of light intertwined in the air, weaving a blurry image—

That was Chen Nian's figure, imprisoned in a dark dungeon. Her wrists and neck were bound by jet-black chains, but her eyes remained clear as ever, gazing toward some direction and murmuring softly.

"Brother..."

That voice was faint and barely audible, yet it clearly entered Chen Ji's ears. In that instant, he felt a sharp pain in his chest—that was the call of blood connection, the voice of his sister he had searched for over the years.

Chen Nian was still alive! And she had been waiting for him all along.

Chen Ji tightly gripped the jade pendant, his knuckles white from force. A resolute light flashed in his eyes—both the coldness of the trash Chen and the ruthlessness of the mastermind.

"Mother, you protected me for ten thousand years. This time, it's my turn to protect Chen Nian."
